name: Zand dynasty (Persia)
summary: The Zand dynasty ruled most of Iran after the fall of Nader Shah’s empire; Karim Khan Zand governed from Shiraz as regent, not shah, and the Qajars replaced the dynasty in 1794.

location.value: Much of Iran (Karim Khan seized power over much of the country). The page does not name Shiraz as capital or say what happened to Khorasan.

terrain.value: Iranian plateau and the Zagros mountains.

climate.value: Dry, with hot summers and cold winters on the Iranian plateau.

resources.value: Farmland, silk, carpets and Persian Gulf trade.

disasters.value: Earthquakes and droughts were recurring dangers on the Iranian plateau.

population.value: The page gives no population figure.

urbanisation.value: Shiraz grew as the capital; Isfahan was still large.

disease.value: Plague outbreaks struck Iranian cities in the late 1700s.

migration.value: Tribal groups moved with Karim Khan’s campaigns.

economicBase.value: Not described on the page; farming, herding and trade need another source.

tradeRoutes.value: Persian Gulf trade through Bushehr, with the British and Dutch East India Companies.

wealth.value: The economy recovered slowly after decades of war and was supported by Gulf trade.

moneyAndTax.value: Silver coins; Karim Khan was known for low taxes.

inequality.value: Tribal chiefs and landholders above peasants.

governmentType.value: The page lists Vakil ol-Ra’aya among the dynasty’s titles; it gives no description of how the state was run.

keyRulers.value: Karim Khan Zand founded the dynasty in 1751 and ruled until 1779. After him came Mohammad-Ali Khan and Abol-Fath Khan (co-rulers, 1779), Sadegh Khan (1779–81), Ali-Morad Khan (1781–85), Jafar Khan (1785–89), Seyd Morad Khan (1789) and Lotf Ali Khan (1789 until deposed in November 1794).

succession.value: After 1779 Mohammad-Ali and Abol-Fath co-ruled, then Sadegh Khan (to 1781), Ali-Morad (1781–85), Jafar (1785–89) and Jafar’s son Lotf Ali, whose reign ended in November 1794.

institutions.value: A tribal confederation of Lurs and Laks.

stability.value: Stable under Karim Khan, then civil war.

eliteConflict.value: Zand princes fought each other and the Qajars.

armyAndTech.value: Tribal cavalry and musketeers, with limited artillery.

majorWars.value: Not described on the page (the Qajar wars and the siege of Basra are not mentioned). The last ruler, Lotf Ali Khan, reigned 1789 to November 1794, when the dynasty was deposed.

territoryChange.value: Held the Ottoman port of Basra from 1776 to 1779.

alliancesRivals.value: The Qajars, Ottomans and Afghans were the main rivals, with the British East India Company active in the Gulf.

scienceEducation.value: Madrasas in Shiraz kept Persian and Islamic learning alive.

openness.value: Open to trade through the Persian Gulf, including the East India Company.

communicationTransport.value: Caravan routes linked Shiraz to Isfahan, Tabriz and Gulf ports.

religion.value: Twelver Shia Islam, according to the infobox.

languageWriting.value: Persian, written in Arabic script, was the language of government and poetry.

artsArchitecture.value: Vakil Mosque, Vakil Bazaar and the Arg of Karim Khan in Shiraz.

socialStructure.value: Tribes, townspeople, merchants and peasants, under a ruling dynasty from the Zand tribe.

sharedIdentity.value: A shared Persian identity, with the Zand rulers presenting themselves as regents.

dailyLife.value: Families lived on bread, rice and tea, and bazaars were the centres of trade and news.

neighbours.value: The Ottomans, the Afghans and the Qajar tribe in the north.

ideasReligions.value: Shia Islam; Shiraz’s poets Hafez and Saadi were honoured.

riseSignals.value: Karim Khan Zand founded the dynasty in 1751 and reigned until 1779, seizing power over much of Iran. The page does not name the capital.

peakPeriod.value: Karim Khan's reign (1751–79). The page names no peak year.

declineSignals.value: The death of Karim Khan in 1779 started succession wars, and the Qajars won in 1794.

outcome.value: The dynasty was deposed in 1794 and the House of Qajar succeeded it.

overallCertainty.value: Main events are well documented; population figures are estimates.
